items.title: Harold Danko interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, April 28, 2021
items.q: Coltrane and whatever, and that was it. It was life-changing.

ctx.x: Well you know that’s about the year I really got interested in jazz and it was thanks to, I had two older brothers, both played saxophone, and so there was jazz in the house but they were much older than me and so they were not living at home, and I was the kid who they would come over and we would play some standard tunes or whatever. I didn’t know much. But then my brother got one of those big stereo things and played “Milestones” actually. And that did it for me. I heard “Milestones” on a stereo where there…

Coltrane and whatever, and that was it. It was life-changing. It might have been, it might have been right in 1959 or ’60 because yeah, it had to be. Because “Milestones” “Kind of Blue” was just going to come out I think. And my brother got me that record for that Christmas. And so all those records you mentioned, plus the rock stuff and all the things I was listening to — I mean Chuck Berry was, you know when I saw him on “American Bandstand” that changed my life too. I saw a guy doing the duck walk or whatever…
